## QUESTION 1

__Calculate the sample size (i.e. number of rows in the dataset) for each airport in each year__. What do you notice?

The highest number in the len column is 12 for 12 months a year, but some airports have less due to having months with no delays—OR SO I THOUGHT. Turns out there are records with a year of "null" that match up with a missing month for a given year. After filling null years with the correct year there are 12 records for each airport.

```{python}
numeric_columns = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("num_of_delays")]


df_atlanta = df.filter((pl.col("airport_code") == "ATL"))

df_filled = df.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("month") == "January")
    .then(pl.col("year").fill_null(strategy="backward"))
    .otherwise(pl.col("year").fill_null(strategy="forward"))
)

df_groups = (
    df_filled.group_by(pl.col("airport_code", "year"))
    .agg(pl.len())
    .sort("airport_code", "year")
)

df_groups
```

## QUESTION 2

__Which airport has the worst delays?__ Describe the metric you chose, and why you chose it to determine the “worst” airport. Your answer should include a summary table that lists (for each airport) the total number of flights, total number of delayed flights, proportion of delayed flights, and average delay time in hours. 

SFO has the worst delays. I corrected for human made delays by removing delays due to weather as weather is not a human controllable variable and I wanted to find the worst run airport with the most delays caused by human error. Interestingly, the average delay per flight at SFO is approximately 15 minutes and 36 seconds; I expected it to be much higher and was surprised to see this. SFO also had the second highest percentage of delayed flights at 10.98%. While ATL has the highest percentage of delayed flights at 11.26% (a 0.28% increase from SFO), they have a significantly lower delay of around 11 minutes and 24 seconds (a ~27% decrease in delay time which is almost 100x the difference of delayed flights) so I would still rank SFO as the worst run airport.

```{python}
df_delayed_proportion = df.with_columns(
    delayed_proportion=pl.col("num_of_delays_total") / pl.col("num_of_flights_total"),
    avg_minutes_delayed_per_flight=pl.col("minutes_delayed_total")
    / pl.col("num_of_flights_total"),
)

df_delays = df_delayed_proportion.select(
    pl.col("airport_code", "delayed_proportion", "avg_minutes_delayed_per_flight")
).sort("avg_minutes_delayed_per_flight", "delayed_proportion", descending=True)

good_months = ["April", "May", "June", "July", "August"]

weather_delays = df.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in(good_months))
    .then(0.40)
    .otherwise(0.65)
    .alias("weather_nas_rate")
)
total_weather_delays = weather_delays.with_columns(
    weather_delay_k=pl.col("num_of_delays_weather")
    + pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft")
    + pl.col("num_of_delays_nas") * pl.col("weather_nas_rate")
)

df_grouped_delays = (
    total_weather_delays.group_by(pl.col("airport_code"))
    .agg(
        (
            pl.col("minutes_delayed_total").sum()
            - pl.col("minutes_delayed_weather").sum()
        ).alias("total_airport_delay_minutes"),
        (pl.col("num_of_delays_total").sum() - pl.col("weather_delay_k").sum())
        .round(0)
        .cast(pl.Int64)
        .alias("total_airport_delays"),
        pl.col("num_of_flights_total").sum().alias("total_airport_flights"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        delayed_flights_percentage=(
            pl.col("total_airport_delays") / pl.col("total_airport_flights") * 100
        ).round(2),
        average_delay_hours_per_flight=(
            (pl.col("total_airport_delay_minutes") / pl.col("total_airport_delays"))
            / 60
        ).round(2),
    )
    .select(
        "airport_code",
        "average_delay_hours_per_flight",
        "total_airport_delays",
        "total_airport_flights",
        "delayed_flights_percentage",
    )
    .sort("average_delay_hours_per_flight", descending=True)
)

# df_delays
df_grouped_delays
```
